title: strong_implies_half_linear: Arithmetic Sufficiency of the Strong Conjecture
content: The proof has four steps: (1) extract `hstrong : diam S ≥ S.card - 1` from the conjecture applied to S, hint, hcard; (2) cast hcard (S.card ≥ 2 : ℕ) to (S.card : ℝ) ≥ 2 via exact_mod_cast; (3) close by linarith, which sees diam ≥ n-1 and n ≥ 2 and derives diam ≥ n/2. The mathematical content: n-1 ≥ n/2 iff n ≥ 2, which holds by hypothesis. The proof reveals that the implication from the strong conjecture to the half-linear bound is purely arithmetic — it contains no geometry at all.
mathContext: The strong conjecture: $\text{diam}(S) \ge |S| - 1$ for any $n$-point integer distance set $S$. Consequence: $\text{diam}(S) \ge n - 1 \ge n/2$ for $n \ge 2$. The constant $1/2$ is not tight — if the strong conjecture holds, one can do better by taking $c = 1 - 1/n \to 1$. But $1/2$ suffices to show linear growth. The exact constant in the conjectured linear bound is unknown.

title: gk_bound_strictly_sublinear: Filters and Asymptotic Comparison
content: The proof uses Mathlib's filter library: `filter_upwards [n_over_log_sublinear 1 (by norm_num)] with n hn` instantiates the parent file's lemma `n_over_log_sublinear 1 : ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n/log n < n*1 = n`, extracting `hn : n/log n < n` for a specific n satisfying the eventual property. Then `rw [mul_one] at hn` simplifies n*1 = n, `rw [mul_div_assoc]` rewrites c*(n/log n), and `exact mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hn hc` scales both sides by c > 0. The `filter_upwards` pattern is a key idiom for eventual properties.
mathContext: For $c > 0$: $cn/\log n < cn \iff n/\log n < n \iff 1/\log n < 1 \iff \log n > 1 \iff n > e$. So the inequality holds for all $n \ge 3$ (since $\log 3 \approx 1.099 > 1$). The `atTop` filter represents 'for all sufficiently large n'. `filter_upwards` converts an eventual property into a for-all-sufficiently-large-n hypothesis. `mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left : a < b → 0 < c → c*a < c*b` is the standard positive-scaling monotonicity lemma.
